name: Processor D
justification: The measured bottleneck is the two-qubit gate count of the ZZ interaction, not routing: Processors A and B both compile the open-chain HVA with 0 routing SWAPs. At N=4,L=2, their CX-RZ-CX ZZ construction uses 12 two-qubit gates, while this native-RZZ design uses 6; for the selected N=4,L=3 circuit the corresponding counts are 18 versus 9. The RZZ basis directly represents each ZZ interaction and halves its modeled two-qubit gate locations without claiming lower error per gate. Rates p1=0.001, p2=0.005, and p_readout=0.01 equal the official minimum allowed synthetic rates; the model assigns RZZ the same p2 as CX/CZ. The six-qubit chorded ring has seven edges, diameter 3, and passes the official 4- and 6-qubit checks. This resource trade-off is not calibrated device evidence and does not model gate-family variation, crosstalk, drift, leakage, or correlated readout.
